bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

						UNIQUE(path)
					);

CREATE TABLE sqlite_sequence(name,seq);

CREATE INDEX index_notes_checksum ON notes (checksum);

CREATE INDEX index_notes_path ON notes (path);

CREATE TABLE links (
						id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT NOT NULL,
						source_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES notes(id)
							ON DELETE CASCADE,
						target_id INTEGER REFERENCES notes(id)
							ON DELETE SET NULL,
						title TEXT DEFAULT('') NOT NULL,
						href TEXT NOT NULL,
						external INT DEFAULT(0) NOT NULL,
						rels TEXT DEFAULT('') NOT NULL,
						snippet TEXT DEFAULT('') NOT NULL
					, snippet_start INTEGER DEFAULT(0) NOT NULL, snippet_end INTEGER DEFAULT(0) NOT NULL, type TEXT DEFAULT('') NOT NULL);

CREATE INDEX index_links_source_id_target_id ON links (source_id, target_id);

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE notes_fts USING fts5(
						path, title, body,
						content = notes,
						content_rowid = id,
						tokenize = "porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 1 tokenchars '''&/'"
					);

CREATE TABLE 'notes_fts_data'(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, block BLOB);

CREATE TABLE 'notes_fts_idx'(segid, term, pgno, PRIMARY KEY(segid, term)) WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TABLE 'notes_fts_docsize'(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sz BLOB);

CREATE TABLE 'notes_fts_config'(k PRIMARY KEY, v) WITHOUT ROWID;

CREATE TRIGGER trigger_notes_ai AFTER INSERT ON notes BEGIN
						INSERT INTO notes_fts(rowid, path, title, body) VALUES (new.id, new.path, new.title, new.body);
					END;

CREATE TRIGGER trigger_notes_ad AFTER DELETE ON notes BEGIN
						INSERT INTO notes_fts(notes_fts, rowid, path, title, body) VALUES('delete', old.id, old.path, old.title, old.body);
					END;

CREATE TRIGGER trigger_notes_au AFTER UPDATE ON notes BEGIN
						INSERT INTO notes_fts(notes_fts, rowid, path, title, body) VALUES('delete', old.id, old.path, old.title, old.body);
						INSERT INTO notes_fts(rowid, path, title, body) VALUES (new.id, new.path, new.title, new.body);
					END;

CREATE TABLE collections (
						id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT NOT NULL,
						kind TEXT NO NULL,
						name TEXT NOT NULL,
						UNIQUE(kind, name)
					);

CREATE INDEX index_collections ON collections (kind, name);

CREATE TABLE notes_collections (
						id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT NOT NULL,
						note_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES notes(id)
							ON DELETE CASCADE,
						collection_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES collections(id)
							ON DELETE CASCADE
					);

CREATE INDEX index_notes_collections ON notes_collections (note_id, collection_id);

CREATE VIEW notes_with_metadata AS
					 SELECT n.*, GROUP_CONCAT(c.name, '') AS tags
					   FROM notes n
					   LEFT JOIN notes_collections nc ON nc.note_id = n.id
					   LEFT JOIN collections c ON nc.collection_id = c.id AND c.kind = 'tag'
					  GROUP BY n.id;

CREATE TABLE metadata (
						key TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
						value TEXT NO NULL
					);

CREATE VIEW resolved_links AS
					 SELECT l.*, s.path AS source_path, s.title AS source_title, t.path AS target_path, t.title AS target_title
					   FROM links l
					   LEFT JOIN notes s ON l.source_id = s.id
					   LEFT JOIN notes t ON l.target_id = t.id;

# Patch parse_toml_config to handle multi-line arrays
_orig_parse_toml_config = parse_toml_config
def parse_toml_config_multiline(text):
    lines = text.split("\n")
    # Pre-process: join lines where brackets unbalanced (for arrays and inline tables)
    joined = []
    buf = ""
    in_array = False
    bracket_depth = 0
    brace_depth = 0
    in_single = False
    in_double = False
    start_lineno = 1
    for lineno, rawline in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        stripped = rawline.strip()
        # If not in array and line is table header or comment/empty, just add
        if not in_array:
            # Check if this line starts a multi-line array/inline table: contains = and then [ or { without closing
            # Find = outside quotes
            eq = find_toml_equals(rawline)
            if eq != -1:
                val_part = rawline[eq+1:].strip()
                # Remove comments? For multi-line detection, need to consider brackets
                # Count brackets in val_part (respecting quotes)
                b, br, sq, dq = count_brackets(val_part)
                if b > 0 or br > 0:
                    # Check if balanced
                    if b != 0 or br != 0:
                        # Start accumulating
                        in_array = True
                        buf = rawline
                        bracket_depth = b
                        brace_depth = br
                        # Track quote state? For simplicity, assume quotes not spanning lines except triple? Triple strings can span lines but rare in config. Ignore.
                        start_lineno = lineno
                        continue
            joined.append((lineno, rawline))
        else:
            buf += "\n" + rawline
            b, br, sq, dq = count_brackets(rawline)
            bracket_depth += b
            brace_depth += br
            if bracket_depth == 0 and brace_depth == 0:
                # End of multi-line
                joined.append((start_lineno, buf))
                buf = ""
                in_array = False
    if in_array:
        joined.append((start_lineno, buf))
    # Now parse joined lines using original logic but with lineno tracking
    root = {}
    current = root
    current_path = []
    defined_tables = set()
    defined_keys = set()
    for lineno, rawline in joined:
        # rawline may contain newlines (for multi-line). For table headers, they are single line, so fine.
        # For key=value with newlines, we need to handle: key is before first =, value is after (including newlines)
        line_stripped_first = rawline.split("\n")[0].strip()
        # Check if it's table header (must be single line, no newline in header)
        if "\n" not in rawline:
            line = rawline.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            if line.startswith("["):
                if not line.endswith("]"):
                    raise TomlError(lineno, len(rawline), "parsing error: unterminated table")
                inner = line[1:-1].strip()
                parts = split_toml_key(inner, lineno)
                tkey = tuple(parts)
                if tkey in defined_tables:
                    raise TomlError(lineno, 1, "duplicated tables")
                defined_tables.add(tkey)
                cur = root
                for p in parts:
                    if p not in cur:
                        cur[p] = {}
                    elif not isinstance(cur[p], dict):
                        raise TomlError(lineno, 1, f"The following key was defined twice: {'.'.join(parts)}")
                    cur = cur[p]
                current = cur
                current_path = parts

            if first_line.strip().startswith("[") or first_line.strip().startswith("#") or not first_line.strip():

                raise TomlError(lineno, 1, "parsing error: unexpected multiline")

            raise TomlError(lineno, 9, f'was expecting token =, but got "{got.strip(chr(34))}" instead')
        key_part = first_line[:eq].strip()

        val_part_full = val_first + "\n" + "\n".join(rest_lines) if rest_lines else val_first
        val_part_full = val_part_full.strip()
        # Remove comments? For arrays, comments inside are allowed? Our array parser handles #? For simplicity, keep as is (array parser will handle)

            val = parse_toml_value(val_part_full, lineno, rawline)
        except TomlError:

        except Exception as e:

        defined_keys.add(full_key)

def count_brackets(s):
    # Returns (bracket_diff, brace_diff, in_single, in_double) ignoring strings
    b = 0
    br = 0
    in_single = False
    in_double = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        c = s[i]
        if in_single:
            if c == "'":
                in_single = False
            i += 1
        elif in_double:
            if c == "\\":
                i += 2
                continue
            elif c == '"':
                in_double = False
            i += 1
        else:
            if c == "'":
                in_single = True
            elif c == '"':
                in_double = True
            elif c == "#":
                break
            elif c == "[":
                b += 1
            elif c == "]":
                b -= 1
            elif c == "{":
                br += 1
            elif c == "}":
                br -= 1
            i += 1
    return b, br, in_single, in_double

def count_brackets(s):
    # Returns (bracket_diff, brace_diff, in_single, in_double) ignoring strings
    b = 0
    br = 0
    in_single = False
    in_double = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        c = s[i]
        if in_single:
            if c == "'":
                in_single = False
            i += 1
        elif in_double:
            if c == "\\":
                i += 2
                continue
            elif c == '"':
                in_double = False
            i += 1
        else:
            if c == "'":
                in_single = True
            elif c == '"':
                in_double = True
            elif c == "#":
                break
            elif c == "[":
                b += 1
            elif c == "]":
                b -= 1
            elif c == "{":
                br += 1
            elif c == "}":
                br -= 1
            i += 1
    return b, br, in_single, in_double

def format_json_time(dt):
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    dt_utc = dt.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc)
    base = dt_utc.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
    us = dt_utc.microsecond
    if us == 0:
        return base + "Z"
    else:
        frac = f"{us:06d}".rstrip("0")
        return f"{base}.{frac}Z"

def format_json_time(dt):
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    dt_utc = dt.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc)
    base = dt_utc.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
    us = dt_utc.microsecond
    if us == 0:
        return base + "Z"
    else:
        frac = f"{us:06d}".rstrip("0")
        return f"{base}.{frac}Z"

def time_ago(dt, now):
    # Replicate zk's relative time: "just now", "X minutes ago", "X hours ago", "X days ago", etc.? Need to determine thresholds.
    # Observed: "just now" for <1 min? "2 minutes ago", "3 minutes ago", "8 minutes ago", etc.
    # What about hours? Days? Weeks? Months? Years? Need to test with older notes (touch file to old date, reindex, check).
    # For now, implement simple: <60s -> "just now", <60m -> "X minutes ago" (or "1 minute ago" singular?), <24h -> "X hours ago", <7d -> "X days ago", <30d -> "X weeks ago"? Or "X days ago"? Need to test.
    # Also need singular vs plural: "1 minute ago" vs "2 minutes ago"? Probably.
    # Let's implement common: just now (<30s? Or <60s?), minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years.
    # To match exactly, need to test with various ages. For now, approximate.
    try:
        delta = (now - dt).total_seconds()
        if delta < 0:
            delta = 0
        if delta < 60:
            return "just now"
        elif delta < 3600:
            m = int(delta // 60)
            return f"{m} minute ago" if m == 1 else f"{m} minutes ago"
        elif delta < 86400:
            h = int(delta // 3600)
            return f"{h} hour ago" if h == 1 else f"{h} hours ago"
        elif delta < 86400*7:
            d = int(delta // 86400)
            return f"{d} day ago" if d == 1 else f"{d} days ago"
        elif delta < 86400*30:
            w = int(delta // (86400*7))
            return f"{w} week ago" if w == 1 else f"{w} weeks ago"
        elif delta < 86400*365:
            mo = int(delta // (86400*30))
            if mo == 0:
                mo = 1
            return f"{mo} month ago" if mo == 1 else f"{mo} months ago"
        else:
            y = int(delta // (86400*365))
            return f"{y} year ago" if y == 1 else f"{y} years ago"
    except:
        return "just now"

def generate_id(charset_name, length, case):
    # charset: letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), alphanum (a-z0-9), hex (a-f0-9), or custom string (any chars)
    if charset_name == "letters":
        chars = string.ascii_lowercase
    elif charset_name == "numbers":
        chars = string.digits
    elif charset_name == "alphanum":
        chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
    elif charset_name == "hex":
        chars = "abcdef0123456789"
    else:
        # Custom string: use as is (e.g., "abc" -> chars "abc")
        chars = charset_name
        if not chars:
            chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
    # Generate random length chars
    res = "".join(random.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))
    # Apply case: lower, upper, mixed
    if case == "lower":
        res = res.lower()
    elif case == "upper":
        res = res.upper()
    elif case == "mixed":
        # Mixed: random case per letter? Or keep as is (since charset may already have mixed? For alphanum lower+digits, mixed would randomly upper some? As observed, mixed gave "Wf1V" (mixed case, with digits). Good. So for mixed, randomly upper/lower each letter (digits unchanged).
        out = ""
        for c in res:
            if c.isalpha():
                out += random.choice([c.lower(), c.upper()])
            else:
                out += c
        res = out
    else:
        res = res.lower()
    return res

def generate_id(charset_name, length, case):
    # charset: letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), alphanum (a-z0-9), hex (a-f0-9), or custom string (any chars)
    if charset_name == "letters":
        chars = string.ascii_lowercase
    elif charset_name == "numbers":
        chars = string.digits
    elif charset_name == "alphanum":
        chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
    elif charset_name == "hex":
        chars = "abcdef0123456789"
    else:
        # Custom string: use as is (e.g., "abc" -> chars "abc")
        chars = charset_name
        if not chars:
            chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
    # Generate random length chars
    res = "".join(random.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))
    # Apply case: lower, upper, mixed
    if case == "lower":
        res = res.lower()
    elif case == "upper":
        res = res.upper()
    elif case == "mixed":
        # Mixed: random case per letter? Or keep as is (since charset may already have mixed? For alphanum lower+digits, mixed would randomly upper some? As observed, mixed gave "Wf1V" (mixed case, with digits). Good. So for mixed, randomly upper/lower each letter (digits unchanged).
        out = ""
        for c in res:
            if c.isalpha():
                out += random.choice([c.lower(), c.upper()])
            else:
                out += c
        res = out
    else:
        res = res.lower()
    return res
